key_insight: A differentiable Schwarz-coupled finite element solver combines near-wall and bulk transport models to support inverse modeling of thin boundary layers with coarser meshes.
engineering_relevance: The framework could reduce computational cost when identifying unknown parameters in high-Péclet transport problems with steep near-wall gradients.
method: Split near-wall and bulk dynamics using perturbation theory and overlapping Schwarz domain decomposition.
Differentiate through coupled FEM solves, enforcing governing equations, boundary conditions, and interface continuity.
Use adjoint sensitivities with an LLM optimizer or a workflow-enabled AI agent that expands a functional basis under a prescribed admission policy.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports lower computational cost than a single-domain formulation and greater agentic AI benefit for functional-basis unknowns than for high-dimensional nodal fields, but provides no quantitative benchmarks.
watch_item: Practical performance may depend on overlap design, mesh resolution, and the basis-admission policy; quantitative accuracy and speedup evidence is needed.
paper_title: Differentiable Schwarz-Coupled Solvers for Thin Boundary Layer Transport: Inverse Modeling via Agentic AI Optimization
